scope: Move the public news site from WordPress (www.lawyard.org, Bluehost) to this application: routes, URLs, taxonomy, editorial surface, SEO continuity, DNS flip and WordPress retirement.
gate: Do not start Phase 3 or later until Tobi answers C0.1 (is the WordPress editor non-negotiable?). The answer picks full cutover vs headless WordPress, and it changes Phase 4 entirely.

baseline_measured.news_front_end: removed in a2869b9 — app/(main) no longer exists
baseline_measured.current_public_site: WordPress on Bluehost; this app serves directory.lawyard.org only
baseline_measured.canonical_taxonomy: drifted once already — CH-077, fixed by 20261122000002..04

assumptions: WordPress remains the editorial source until the flip, so it can be read from during the build
Search equity is worth protecting: 11k URLs are the asset, not the design
One engineer plus Tobi's editorial time; effort is engineer-hours unless stated
The directory keeps shipping independently — cutover must not block marketplace work
Headless WordPress is a legitimate outcome, not a failure; it changes Phase 4 only
definition_of_done: www.lawyard.org serves this app; 20 sampled legacy URLs 301 to the right canonical URL
GA4 and Search Console continuity preserved through the flip
Editorial team can publish, schedule, edit and unpublish without WordPress
WordPress remains reachable read-only for 12 months, then is decommissioned
Rollback rehearsed and documented with a measured time-to-restore

title: Answer the one question that forks the plan: is the WordPress editor non-negotiable?
why: Full cutover and headless WordPress share Phases 1-3 and differ completely in Phase 4. Deciding late wastes the most expensive work.
steps: Ask Tobi directly; frame it as a newsroom question, not a technology one
If yes → headless: WordPress stays the authoring UI, this app renders. Phase 4 becomes an API integration, not an editor build
If no → full cutover: Content Studio becomes the newsroom tool and must be good enough before the flip
Record the answer and the rejected option in docs/OPERATIONS.md
acceptance: Decision recorded with date and rationale
Phase 4 shape chosen
rollback: Decision can be revisited, but not cheaply after Phase 4 starts.

title: Agree what 'migrated' means, in numbers
why: Without an agreed target, the flip becomes an argument about taste. With one, it is a checklist.
steps: Agree the URL survival bar (e.g. 99% of published permalinks resolve to 200 or 301-to-relevant)
Agree the content bar: 11,306 published posts render, with images, alt text and working internal links
Agree the editorial bar: publish, schedule, edit, unpublish — in the new tool, without WordPress
Write the three bars into the plan header before any build
acceptance: Three measurable bars written down and signed off by Tobi

title: Confirm the media dependency is actually closed
why: Routes can be restored in a day; media cannot. Phase 2 must not start on a host that still hotlinks WordPress.
steps: Run the zero-reference gate from media-storage-v1 M5.1
Confirm the 301 tail for wp-content/** is live
Link the media plan's completion record into this plan
acceptance: All media-count queries return 0
Legacy image URL sample returns 301

title: Export the full URL corpus from WordPress, not from memory
why: The redirect map is only as good as the URL list. Sitemap exports miss paginated archives, feeds and author pages.
steps: Pull wp-json/wp/v2/posts, /pages, /categories, /tags and the sitemap index
Include archive shapes: /page/n, /author/*, /category/*/page/n, date archives, feeds
Record counts per shape before designing the map
acceptance: Every URL shape the site currently answers is in one list with a count
Total published post URLs reconciles with 11,306

title: Map taxonomy from WordPress terms to the canonical registry
why: Taxonomy has already drifted once (CH-077). A second mapping done by hand will drift again.
steps: Export WP categories/tags with post counts
Map each to the canonical practice areas/categories in lib/directory/practice-areas.ts and the articles.category values
Flag terms with no canonical equivalent rather than inventing one
acceptance: Every published post resolves to at least one canonical category
Unmapped terms listed with counts
rollback: Mapping is data; revert the file.

title: Decide the fate of comments, users and subscribers
why: They are the parts of a news site that nobody remembers until they are gone, and each has a different legal and practical weight.
steps: Count WP comments and identify whether they are imported, archived or dropped (with Tobi)
Identify subscriber source of truth (Brevo vs WP) and confirm no double-send risk
Decide what happens to WP user accounts (authors, commenters)
acceptance: A written decision per surface: import, archive, drop
No surface left implicit

title: Restore the news routes in this app
why: app/(main) was deleted in a2869b9. Without it there is nothing to flip to — this is the actual migration.
steps: Restore insights index + [slug], category, search, podcasts, TV, legislations, about/contact and the RSS feed
Reuse the article template already built and hardened for corporate posts (sanitiser, typography, ad slots)
Wire the routes to the existing getPublishedArticles/getArticleBySlug helpers rather than new queries
acceptance: A published article renders end to end on a preview host with images, alt text and ads
Homepage and category archive render with pagination
rollback: Revert the commit; the directory is unaffected.

title: Build the 301 map from the URL corpus
why: 11,306 URLs are the SEO asset. A flip without a complete map trades a working archive for a redirect error page.
steps: Generate path → new path for posts (slug preserved), categories, tags, authors, pagination
Choose one canonical shape per concept and redirect every alias to it (no chains)
Implement as edge redirects with the map generated from data, not typed by hand
Test 20 samples covering: post, category page 2, author, feed, unknown path
acceptance: 20/20 sampled legacy URLs 301 to a relevant 200
No redirect chains longer than one hop
rollback: Remove the redirect rule; WordPress still serves.

title: Normalise imported content: shortcodes, more-tags, internal links
why: The bodies carry WordPress machinery and point at the old host. This is the same rewrite class as media and is already measured.
steps: Reuse media-storage-v1 M2.5/M2.6 output — do not rewrite bodies twice
Verify internal links resolve to canonical new URLs before flip, not after
Confirm the sanitiser allowlist covers everything the rewrite produces
acceptance: Zero shortcodes and more-tags in published bodies
Internal link sample resolves to 200 from the preview host
verify_sql: select count(*) from articles where content like '%<!--more-->%';

title: Add article structured data and social metadata
why: NewsArticle schema and correct og:image are how the archive keeps its search and social surface. The directory app already sets some of this; the news template must too.
steps: Emit NewsArticle JSON-LD with headline, author, datePublished, dateModified, image
Emit canonical URLs and og/twitter cards per article
Validate 3 samples in a structured-data checker and a link preview debugger
acceptance: No structured-data errors on 3 sampled articles
og:image resolves absolutely and is >=1200px wide

title: Verify the 284 non-published rows behave
why: Drafts, pending and scheduled rows are the pipeline. If the new site cannot represent them, editors lose work they can see in WordPress.
steps: Confirm draft/pending rows are invisible publicly and visible to editors
Confirm scheduled publishing still fires (the cron/edge function already exists)
Confirm unpaid corporate posts never publish
acceptance: Draft is publicly 404 and editorially visible
A scheduled row publishes on time
An unpaid corporate post stays unpublished

title: Preserve GA4 and Search Console continuity
why: Analytics that restart at zero make the migration look like a traffic collapse, and break the year-over-year case Tobi sells with.
steps: Decide: reuse the existing GA4 property (recommended) or start a new one with a migration annotation
Add GA4 to this app only at cutover, so the two hosts never double-count
Add Search Console verification for the new host before flip; keep the old property for the 12-month tail
acceptance: Property verified on the new host before flip
No period where both hosts report to the same property
rollback: Remove the tag; WordPress keeps reporting.

title: Sitemap, robots and feeds cover the whole archive
why: The current sitemap deliberately lists directory pages only. A news cutover without an article sitemap invites slow re-indexing.
steps: Extend app/sitemap.ts to include news articles when the news routes ship, paging past PostgREST's 1,000-row cap
Point robots.txt at it; keep ads.txt untouched
Validate in Search Console after flip
acceptance: Sitemap lists all published articles plus directory pages
Sitemap count reconciles with published count
verify_sql: select count(*) from articles where status = 'published'; -- must match sitemap count
rollback: Revert the commit; directory sitemap unaffected.

title: Baseline the rankings and traffic you are risking
why: You cannot claim the migration preserved SEO without a before-picture, and you cannot spot a real drop against a flat baseline.
steps: Export 30 days of Search Console queries/pages and GA4 sessions before the flip
Record top 50 landing pages and their positions
Re-measure at +7, +30 and +90 days
acceptance: Baseline file stored with the migration docs
Two follow-up checkpoints scheduled

title: Make the editorial surface good enough for a newsroom (full cutover only)
why: This is where migrations usually fail: the front end is right and the writers refuse to use it. Skip if C0.1 chose headless.
steps: Publish, edit, schedule, unpublish and preview — all without a deploy
Inline images with alt text; revisions or at least an undo path
Slack review flow already exists — confirm it covers news articles, not just corporate posts
acceptance: A non-technical editor publishes a post with an image unaided
An accidental publish can be reverted without engineering
rollback: WordPress stays the authoring surface until this passes.

title: Build the headless path instead, if C0.1 says the WP editor stays
why: The coherent version of 'keep WordPress': it authors, this app renders. Two front ends is not an option.
steps: Create/keep a WP application password and expose only the fields the renderer needs
Revalidate the affected paths on publish (webhook → on-demand revalidation)
Keep the archive in Supabase as the read model; WP remains the write model
acceptance: A post published in WordPress appears on the new site within one revalidation cycle
No second public front end exists
rollback: Point the front end back at WordPress.

title: Train and hand over the newsroom
why: The tool is not migrated until the people are.
steps: One 45-minute session with Tobi's team, recorded
A one-page cheat sheet: publish, schedule, edit, unpublish, add an image
A named owner for the first week of questions
acceptance: Team publishes one real article unaided before the flip

title: Stand up a preview host and make Tobi sign off on real pages
why: Nobody should discover the new news site on flip day. A preview host turns opinion into a diff.
steps: Deploy the news routes to next.lawyard.org (or a Vercel preview with a stable alias)
Send Tobi 5 real articles, one category page and the homepage
Collect a written go/no-go with named defects
acceptance: Tobi's sign-off recorded, or the defect list becomes tasks

title: Rehearse the rollback before you need it
why: A rollback plan nobody has run is a hope. The flip is only safe if going back is boring.
steps: Document the DNS revert to Bluehost with TTLs and exact records
Time the revert end to end in a rehearsal
Define the trigger conditions for reverting (e.g. >5% of sampled URLs broken, checkout or publish failure)
acceptance: Measured time-to-restore recorded
Trigger conditions agreed with Tobi

title: Load-test the news routes before flip day
why: The archive is 11k pages behind one Next deploy; a crawler hitting it cold is the most predictable traffic spike you will get.
steps: Crawl the full sitemap against the preview host at a polite rate
Watch function duration, DB pool usage and image egress
Fix any page that times out or exceeds its budget
acceptance: Full sitemap crawl completes with no 5xx
P95 page response within budget under crawl

title: Run the flip as a checklist, not as a deploy
why: The flip is a sequence with an order that matters: freeze, final sync, DNS, verify, then unpark WordPress read-only.
steps: Freeze publishing in WordPress and take a final content + media delta
Flip DNS for www to the new host; keep TTLs low from C5.2
Verify: homepage, 5 articles, category page, RSS, sitemap, one corporate post, one ad slot
Switch WordPress to read-only and keep it reachable for the 12-month tail
acceptance: All verification URLs return 200 with correct content
Publishing works on the new host
WordPress unreachable for writes
rollback: DNS revert per C5.2; measured, rehearsed.

title: Watch the first 72 hours
why: Redirect gaps, image 404s and indexation problems show up as a trickle in the first three days, not on day one.
steps: Daily: crawl 200 random legacy URLs, check 404 rate in logs
Check Search Console coverage errors and GA4 traffic against the C3.3 baseline
Fix redirect gaps same-day; each is a ranking at risk
acceptance: No unresolved redirect gap older than 24h
Traffic within the agreed band of baseline at +7 days
rollback: Revert per C5.2 if the trigger fires.

title: Retire WordPress on a schedule, not on a whim
why: The old host is the backup. Deleting it the week after the flip removes the only safety net and the media tail.
steps: Keep WordPress read-only, and wp-content/uploads/** redirects, for 12 months
At +12 months: archive the database and uploads to cold storage, then decommission
Remove the redirect tail only after Search Console shows the new URLs indexing
acceptance: Calendar reminders for +7d, +90d, +12m
Decommission checklist includes a cold archive
rollback: Not applicable after decommission — which is why it waits 12 months.

title: Record the outcome in the repository
why: The next session inherits the record, not the reasoning in someone's head.
steps: Update docs/CUTOVER.md from parked plan to completed record with actual dates and counts
Log the session in docs/data/timeline.json with before/after numbers
Note what was deliberately dropped (comments, shortcodes, etc.) and why
acceptance: pnpm docs:check passes
CUTOVER.md no longer says 'parked' or explains exactly why it still is
